exposure: labor and delivery unit capacity and staffing
regular provision of feedback on cesarean rates and indications to physicians
regular review of cesarean rates and indications
regular review of vaginal birth after cesarean rates
permitting women to eat during labor
cesarean at the request of the woman
blood draw for complete blood count/type and antibody screen
outcome: association between hospital characteristics and intrapartum practices with cesarean rate
cohort: Nurse managers or other clinical staff knowledgeable about intrapartum care from 39 hospitals (out of 60 eligible) in Connecticut and Massachusetts
finding: Intrapartum practices varied markedly across hospitals, with some practices (e.g., offering cesarean on request, liberal indications for induction and cesarean) associated with higher cesarean rates, while others (e.g., having certified nurse-midwives, permitting eating during labor) were associated with lower rates.
mod_finding: Hospitals that allowed cesarean delivery at the request of the woman and had more liberal indications for labor induction and cesarean birth had significantly higher cesarean rates; conversely, having a certified nurse-midwife consistently available and allowing women to eat during labor were associated with lower cesarean rates.
